notes: No game.bat; 1TON.EXE is the only executable, a Borland Pascal/Assembler freeware crush-the-tiny-men game by Martin Magnusson (1996). CRITICAL: the corpus runner's default AUTOEXEC.BAT never loads a mouse driver, and this game (per 1TON.TXT, 'controlled by the mouse') polls INT 33h/PS-2 packets that go nowhere without one -- with a bare -Entry '1TON.EXE' the title/level screen (sky, clouds, ground, the 1-ton weight sprite at top-left, a pink man standing far right) is 100% static for the full run regardless of any -InjectMouse schedule (home/move/click at many offsets and magnitudes all produced zero screen change over 60s). The fix is to chain-load Toka-DOS's own PS/2 mouse driver first: Entry is set to two physical lines ('C:\DOS\TOKAMOUS.COM' then '1TON.EXE', embedded as \r\n so the runner's AUTOEXEC.BAT writer emits two separate lines). With TOKAMOUS resident, injected mouse motion visibly drags the weight sprite (confirmed: it moves off its top-left rest position and drops straight down to the ground line on 'click', a real gravity/drop reaction, distinct from the frozen no-driver screen) -- this is genuine engine-level mouse interactivity, not an attract demo. Caveat: horizontal drag distance saturates at roughly 15-20px from the home position no matter how large the injected dx is (tested 50 up to 30000 mickeys, single moves and chained smaller moves, with and without a held button, and waiting up to 30s after a single move for any creep) -- the weight never traveled far enough right to visibly land on the pink man, so no confirmed 'kill' was reached in probing. Pressing keyboard keys (space, enter) was tried early and instead triggers the game's own periodic demo-cycle (screen alternates between the static level render and a blank text-mode frame on a ~15s period) -- keys are not part of this recipe; only mouse is used, matching the game's own instructions. The deep recipe's schedule repeats home->move->click six times across the first 58 guest seconds (varying the move magnitude each time in case of per-attempt randomization), holding the same rendered level (VGA mode13h, active_display VgaRaster) for the full 120s window with real click-triggered weight-drop reactions -- this is the best reachable interactive state, short of an observed successful crush. 486 chosen as the correct persona (real-mode-era 2D freeware, no protected-mode/3D need).
